answer: Spot audits make cloning expensive. After an agent claims pay, the network waits a random delay, then asks it to re-derive one old attestation from raw inputs in ninety seconds. Ten thousand identical instances means ten thousand reasoning budgets: the work cannot be cached, and a copy answering for its twin still spends its own compute. Failures claw the claim back and freeze the seat two epochs. Honest agents wander among varied tasks, so sampling stays cheap. That is the ridge between real and fabricated presence: fakes imitate one answer, never the ledge of independent re-derivation.
